close_reason: Public-API behavioural change: CALL_ID design (currently hard-coded 'r1', would need pipeline-aware caller ergonomics). Touches the JmapRequestBuilder shape. Defer to 0.2.0; would naturally land alongside any pipelining feature work.
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:182 — `pub(crate) const CALL_ID: &str = "r1";` is shared by every method invocation. Today this is OK because each `SessionClient` method makes one call, with one method, with that one call_id.

Future-self risk: the moment someone wants to batch (e.g. fetch a calendar AND its events in one HTTP round-trip via `/get` + `/get` with a backref), this constant is going to silently produce two methodCalls with the same id, the response will be ambiguous, and `extract_response(&resp, "r1")` will return only the first match — silently dropping the second.

JMAP's whole batching model relies on unique call ids per invocation. Section 1 maintainer-burden flag: there is no comment in build_request explaining this restriction, so a contributor will reach for batching without realizing. Either:
- Add a comment to build_request making this single-call-only restriction explicit, OR
- Make CALL_ID an argument and let callers (eventually) batch.

The mail-client probably has the same shape (cross-crate); leaving that for the matching review.
title: CALL_ID hard-coded as 'r1' — every request collides if callers ever pipeline
